_what: The tables the person's files keep their names index in (src/store/mod.rs reads this once). Each table mirrors the column list of the archive table of the same name (ns_name, ns_folder, ns_file, ns_chunk, ns_alias, ns_spans), so the account owner's rows copy in with one INSERT ... SELECT: the archive's id and columns, plus `scope` (which scope a row is in: the names of one folder, the one files scope, and so on), `version`, and the two request columns, which a copy fills as the SELECT in README.md shows. A record is one flat object: a field whose value fits its column's kind lives in that column, any other field lives in `extra` (a JSON object), so no record loses a field. A scope no table claims is kept in `generic`. `minted` names a whole-number column the store itself fills: a new row whose value does not carry it gets the change order of the change that made it, a row that came in without one (a copy, or a table from before) gets the next numbers when the store is opened, a changed row keeps the one it has, and a removed row's tombstone keeps it, so it is the row's stable id across everything that carries the value to another id (a rename carries it; a copy leaves it out and gets its own). Every row and every tombstone also keeps `changed`, the store's change order of its last change (one order for the whole store, `ns_order`), which is what a walk of changes after a cursor reads.
id_collation: Ids compare as bytes, in every database, so a page's order is the same everywhere.
